sources.note: 1-page PDF, footer 'Uppdaterad december 2024', still the train map linked from skanetrafiken.se/kartor/ on 29 Aug 2026. Legend has five station classes: Pågatågen; Öresunds- och Pågatågen; Krösatågen; Öresunds- och Krösatågen; Öresunds-, Påga- och Krösatågen. Malmö C, Triangeln, Hyllie, Burlöv, Lund C all print the 'Öresunds- och Pågatågen' symbol — Öresundståg overlap at Triangeln/Hyllie/Burlöv is CONFIRMED, not just at Malmö C. Östervärn, Rosengård, Persborg, Svågertorp, Oxie print the Pågatågen-only symbol. Ring topology visible: Malmö C – Östervärn – Rosengård – Persborg – (junction) – Svågertorp – Hyllie – Triangeln – Malmö C. Arrows: 'mot Danmark' west of Hyllie (Öresund), 'mot Göteborg' north of Halmstad, 'mot Växjö/Kalmar' beyond Älmhult, 'mot Karlskrona' east of Karlshamn. The map draws NO line numbers — it is product-level, not line-level; per-line structure below comes from the GTFS Sweden 3 pattern analysis cross-checked against this map's geography.

notes: D1 oracle upgraded 29 Aug 2026: the official Skånetrafiken train map ('Fler resmöjligheter med tåg', Uppdaterad december 2024) was obtained and hand-checked — the egress block that forced the first pass to hand-transcribe from GTFS alone is gone. Station geography and per-station product symbols come from that map; per-line ordered stops/termini come from GTFS Sweden 3 pattern analysis (3,244 Pågatåg trips) cross-checked against the map — every station in lines[] appears on the map with a Pågatågen symbol.

LINE-CODE RESOLUTION: Pågatågen has NO passenger-facing line codes. The official map draws no line numbers; skanetrafiken.se names services by corridor ('Pågatågen mellan Helsingborg och Åstorp') and individual trains by train number ('Pågatåg 1739'); the GTFS feed's route_short_name is the train number. The first pass's hedged 'H3, H4, E6, etc.' convention is WRONG — no such codes exist. The numeric ids used by reference sources (2–11, incl. 4B) are planning/reference numbers only, stored below as referenceLineNumber, never a chip token.

LINE-COUNT CORRECTION: the first pass's 'eleven core lines + rush-hour-only line 12' is not supported by any source found. The network is 10 service corridors (reference numbers 2, 3, 4B, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 — no 1, no 12), where 2+6 and 4B+9 through-run as single services and 10 is the limited-daily PågatågenExpress. 'Line 12' appears nowhere; the closest real thing is PågatågenExpress (Malmö Svågertorp–Hässleholm, plus Älmhult through trips; reduced in summer).

MALMÖRINGEN RESOLVED — AND THE OSLO-LINE-5 HAZARD IS REAL, AT MALMÖ C ITSELF: the ring is Malmö C – Östervärn – Rosengård – Persborg – Svågertorp – Hyllie – Triangeln – Malmö C, run in BOTH directions, and through-runs to/from Kävlinge via Lomma (Lommabanan). 142 GTFS trips call Malmö C twice on one through-path (Kävlinge → … → Malmö C → ring → Malmö C), exactly like Oslo line 5 at Stortinget. Worse: stop_headsign is 'Malmö central' at every call, INCLUDING trains departing Malmö C outbound around the ring — destination-only direction labeling is broken on this line at the hub lock itself. No OTHER station is called twice on any pattern.

Öresundståg overlap CONFIRMED at Triangeln, Hyllie, AND Burlöv (map legend symbol 'Öresunds- och Pågatågen'), not just Malmö C. doNotGroup the Pågatågen stop vs the Öresundståg stop at all four. Öresundståg itself stays out of v1.
Burlöv and Oxie CONFIRMED in v1: both print Pågatågen symbols on the official map and both appear in current GTFS service (Burlöv on lines 3/6/8/9/10 patterns; Oxie on line 6).

Scope correction from the expansion tracker stands: Malmö has no active light rail/tram (closed 1973; seasonal museum tram only, not v1). V1 is Pågatågen commuter rail only. No bus, no Öresundståg, no Krösatågen (Krösatågen-only stations like Killeberg/Osby/Hästveda/Ballingslöv are on the map but are NOT v1 rows).
City id malmo is separate from goteborg (Västtrafik) and stockholm. Do not merge.

Hub lock Malmö C (Citytunneln portal, opened Dec 2010). Lines 3, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11 all call it — the 'all or most lines' claim is now concrete: 6 of 10 corridors (the other 4 are the north/east corridors that never enter Malmö).

Feed-vs-print renames (GTFS Sweden 3 stop_name vs official map string): 'Malmö Centralstation'→'Malmö C', 'Malmö Triangeln'→'Triangeln', 'Malmö Hyllie'→'Hyllie', 'Malmö Svågertorp'→'Svågertorp', 'Malmö Persborg'→'Persborg', 'Malmö Rosengård station'→'Rosengård', 'Lund Gunnesbo station'→'Gunnesbo', 'Trelleborg C'→'Trelleborg', 'Sölvesborgs Resecentrum'→'Sölvesborg', 'Karlshamn Resecentrum'→'Karlshamn', 'Laholm Station'→'Laholm', '<name> station' suffix elsewhere. lines[].stations use the printed map strings; see the oracle report's rename table.

gtfsRouteIdsIfKnown is empty on every line by necessity, not omission: the national feed has no stable line-level route ids (one route id per train number, e.g. 9011790000000000-1739). Route-id mapping is Jim's D2+ concern against whichever feed he wires.
Trafiklab licenses captured (see oracle report License section): GTFS Sweden 3 and GTFS Regional are both CC0 1.0 Universal — redistribution/commercial use unrestricted, no attribution required.

RESOLVED 29 Aug 2026 (kept for the record): direction wording verified against Skånetrafiken's own journey API (gw-tps/api/v2/Journey, live 29 Aug 2026). The line object carries towards: 'mot Kävlinge' for a ring departure at Malmö C (train 1420: Malmö C Spår 11 → Östervärn → ring → Malmö C Spår 3a → Lomma → Kävlinge, 'mot Kävlinge' the whole way) and buses show 'mot Stenkällan via Rosengård' — the convention is 'mot <far end>' with optional 'via'.
